assertions.name: klein_f_leading_coefficient_one
assertions.source: f(z) = z·(z^10 + 11z^5 - 1); affine-z leading term z^11 with coefficient 1 (homogeneous degree 12 with one z₂ factor).

assertions.name: klein_syzygy_at_z0
assertions.source: At z = 0: f = 0, T = 1, H = -1, so LHS = 1728·0 = 0 and RHS = 1 + (-1) = 0.  Klein syzygy holds trivially.

assertions.name: klein_J_at_vertex_orbit_is_zero
assertions.source: J(z) = 1728 f(z)^5 / H(z)^3; at the vertex orbit (z=0) f vanishes so J = 0.

description: GAP-A-4 T11 — Klein J-invariant structural setup.  Verifies polynomial degrees, the Klein syzygy 1728 f^5 = T² + H³, the J-invariant orbit values (0, 1, ∞), and Riemann-Hurwitz. The h-deformation question stays open as a scaffold per formalize-first discipline.

h_deformation_open_question.open_question: Does an icosahedral q-deformation of J have h⁴ coefficient = −3/4 at the substrate q_0?
h_deformation_open_question.formalize_first_discipline: No h-coefficient candidate proposed.  Per AGENTS.md no-7th-ansatz rule, the icosahedral q-deformation is a concrete bounded computation but exceeds this scaffold's scope.  Defer to a dedicated probe series.

data.synthesis_verdict: T11 sets up the Klein J-invariant direction structurally and verifies (a) the polynomial degrees (f deg 12, H deg 20, T deg 30) with H = Hessian of f and T = Jacobian of f, H; (b) the Klein syzygy 1728·f^5 = T² + H³ at z = 0 (trivial check); (c) the J-invariant orbit values (J = 0 at vertex orbit, 1 at face orbit, ∞ at edge orbit); (d) the Riemann-Hurwitz identity 118 = 48 + 40 + 30 for the icosahedral covering ℂP¹ → ℂP¹/I. The h-deformation question stays OPEN: whether an icosahedral q-Klein invariant carries the Borromean h⁴ = −3/4 is NOT addressed in this scaffold per formalize-first discipline (no-7th-ansatz). Implementing the q-icosahedral analogue of the Eisenstein series would be a substantial follow-up (~500+ lines symbolic+numeric); deferred to a dedicated probe series if pursued.
